1	# Key Data Flows — MCP Server GUI
     2	
     3	---
     4	
     5	## 1. Server Startup
     6	
     7	```
     8	main()
     9	  ├── Parse CLI args (--port, --ledger-dir)
    10	  ├── resolveLedgerRoot() → ledgerRoot path
    11	  ├── readConfigFromDisk(configPath) → populate config cache
    12	  ├── startConfigWatcher(configPath) → fs.watch for external changes
    13	  ├── startAutoArchiveTimer() → periodic project archival
    14	  ├── captureWorkspaceVersions() → snapshot boot versions (for stale detection)
    15	  └── createServer(handleRequest).listen(port)
    16	        → Log "MCP GUI server running at http://localhost:{port}"
    17	```
    18	
    19	---
    20	
    21	## 2. Request Lifecycle
    22	
    23	```
    24	Incoming HTTP Request
    25	  │
    26	  ├── OPTIONS → 200 (CORS preflight)
    27	  │
    28	  ├── Non-API path (no /api prefix)
    29	  │   └── serveStatic(req, res)
    30	  │       ├── Resolve file path in PUBLIC_DIR
    31	  │       ├── Prevent path traversal (resolved must start with PUBLIC_DIR)
    32	  │       ├── Read file → send with MIME type + security headers
    33	  │       └── Not found → 404 JSON error
    34	  │
    35	  └── API path (/api/...)
    36	      ├── Declarative route table (PUT, PATCH, POST with body, and body-free variants with noBody:true)
    37	      │   ├── dispatchRoute(req, res, method, url, port, buildRoutes(...))
    38	      │   │   ├── parseQueryString(url) → URLSearchParams (passed as 3rd handler arg)
    39	      │   │   ├── Match Route[] table (method + path/RegExp; noBody:true skips body read)
    40	      │   │   ├── readJsonBody(req) — enforce 1 MiB limit (skipped when noBody:true)
    41	      │   │   ├── route.handler(body, groups?, query?) → result
    42	      │   │   └── sendJson(res, statusCode ?? 200, result) | writeHead(204) + res.end()
    43	      │   └── Returns true → handleRequest returns
    44	      │
    45	      └── Body-free GET / DELETE routes (matchRoute fallback)
    46	          ├── matchRoute(method, url, ledgerRoot, orchestratorLogsDir)
    47	          │   ├── Parse URL segments
    48	          │   ├── Match against route table (segment count + values)
    49	          │   └── Return handler thunk or null
    50	          ├── handler() → result
    51	          └── sendJson(res, 200, result)
    52	
    53	Error handling (any path):
    54	  ApiError           → sendError(res, statusFromCode, code, message)
    55	  PayloadTooLargeError → sendError(res, 413, ...)
    56	  Unhandled          → stderr log + sendError(res, 500, 'INTERNAL_ERROR', ...)
    57	```
    58	
    59	---
    60	
    61	## 3. Client-Side SPA Boot Sequence
    62	
    63	```
    64	Browser loads index.html
    65	  │
    66	  ├── <head>: theme-init.js executes synchronously
    67	  │   └── Read localStorage('mcp-theme')
    68	  │       └── Set <html data-theme="dark"> (or remove for light)
    69	  │       → Prevents flash of unstyled content (FOUC)
    70	  │
    71	  ├── <body>: Scripts load in order (all synchronous)
    72	  │   ├── marked.min.js → window.marked
    73	  │   ├── api-client.js → window.API
    74	  │   ├── theme.js → window.Theme
    75	  │   ├── router.js → window.Router
    76	  │   ├── utils.js → window.escapeHtml, formatDate, breadcrumb, showLoading,
    77	  │   │             showError (→ UI.banner('error', …) since rework-1), etc.
    78	  │   ├── components.js → window.UI
    79	  │   ├── views/project-detail-helpers.js → helpers (STAGE_ABBREV, buildPipelineTrack, etc.)
    80	  │   ├── views/project-detail-orch.js   → renderOrchToolbar, renderRunsList, etc.
    81	  │   ├── views/project-detail-modal.js  → PIPELINE_STAGES, showResetModal
    82	  │   ├── views/project-detail.js + other views/*.js → window.renderProjectList, etc.
    83	  │   │   (project-detail sub-modules must be loaded before project-detail.js — see §3a)
    84	  │   ├── orchestrator-widgets.js → window.OrchestratorWidgets
    85	  │   ├── stale-check.js → window.StaleCheck
    86	  │   └── app.js → Bootstrap
    87	  │
    88	  └── app.js executes:
    89	      ├── Theme.init() → bind toggle button, apply stored theme
    90	      ├── Router.init() → listen hashchange, dispatch current hash
    91	      └── StaleCheck.init() → start 30s polling of /api/server-info
    92	```
    93	
    94	---
    95	
    96	## 3a. project-detail Module Load Order
    97	
    98	`project-detail.js` is decomposed into four files that must be loaded in dependency order. `index.html` and all 9 GUI test files enforce this sequence:
    99

1	# Constraints & Conventions — MCP Server GUI
     2	
     3	---
     4	
     5	## 1. No Build Step
     6	
     7	The frontend has **zero build tooling**. All `.js` and `.css` files in `public/` are served as-is by the static file server. There is no bundler, no minifier, no transpiler, no source maps.
     8	
     9	**Implications:**
    10	- Do not use `import`/`export` syntax in frontend files.
    11	- Do not use `let`, `const`, arrow functions, template literals, or other ES6+ features in frontend code.
    12	- Do not add a `package.json` to `gui/` or `gui/public/`.
    13	- Do not introduce webpack, vite, rollup, esbuild, or any bundler.
    14	- Cache-busting is done manually via `?v=N` query strings in `index.html` script/link tags.
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## 2. ES5-Compatible JavaScript (Frontend)
    19	
    20	All frontend JavaScript uses **ES5-compatible patterns**:
    21	
    22	- `var` instead of `let`/`const`.
    23	- `function` declarations instead of arrow functions.
    24	- String concatenation instead of template literals.
    25	- IIFE module pattern instead of ES modules.
    26	- `Promise` chains with `.then()` / `.catch()` (native Promises are the one ES6 feature used, as all target browsers support them).
    27	
    28	**Exception:** `async/await` appears in `api-client.js` internal helper — this is acceptable because the GUI targets modern browsers where async/await has been supported since 2017.
    29	
    30	**Rationale:** The codebase was designed for maximum simplicity and zero dependencies. The pattern is intentional — do not "upgrade" to modern syntax without adding a transpilation step.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## 3. Global Namespace Pattern
    35	
    36	Frontend modules expose their public API as global variables via IIFEs:
    37	
    38	```javascript
    39	var ModuleName = (function () {
    40	  // private
    41	  return { publicMethod: fn };
    42	})();
    43	```
    44	
    45	**Rules:**
    46	- Each file exposes exactly one namespace (or a set of bare functions for `utils.js`).
    47	- Dependencies between modules are implicit (load order in `index.html` matters).
    48	- View files expose a `render*` function that the router calls.
    49	- Do not introduce a module loader or import map.
    50	
    51	**Cross-module shared state (`globalThis`):** When a view is split into sub-modules that need to share a mutable array or object, the owning module declares it as a `var` and immediately promotes it to `globalThis`:
    52	
    53	```javascript
    54	// In the owning module (project-detail.js):
    55	var _pdLogPreviewCleanups = [];
    56	globalThis._pdLogPreviewCleanups = _pdLogPreviewCleanups;
    57	```
    58	
    59	Sub-modules then reference the shared state exclusively via `globalThis.*`. All in-place mutations (`.push()`, `.length = 0`) operate on the same array instance.
    60	
    61	**Drain invariant:** Drain sites must use `.length = 0` (in-place reset), never `= []` (reassignment). Reassignment would create a new array that the other module's reference does not see, silently breaking the drain contract. See `data-flows.md §3a` for the full project-detail module load-order and shared-state documentation.
    62	
    63	---
    64	
    65	## 4. Hash-Based Routing Convention
    66	
    67	- All client-side routes use `#` prefix (e.g., `#/projects/repo/slug`).
    68	- The router matches routes via regex patterns in declaration order.
    69	- Route parameters are extracted via capture groups.
    70	- All URL parameters passed to API calls must be `encodeURIComponent()`-encoded.
    71	- New routes must be added to **both** `router.js` (dispatch) and the corresponding view file.
    72	
    73	---
    74	
    75	## 5. View Module Naming
    76	
    77	| Convention | Example |
    78	|------------|---------|
    79	| File name | `views/{noun}.js` (hyphenated) |
    80	| Render function | `render{PascalCase}(app, ...params)` |
    81	| First argument | Always the `#app` container element |
    82	| Pattern | `showLoading()` → fetch → build HTML string → set innerHTML |
    83	
    84	Views must:
    85	- Call `showLoading(app)` before any async work.
    86	- Handle fetch errors with `showError(app, message)`.
    87	- Use `breadcrumb()` for navigation context.
    88	- Cache project names via `ProjectNameCache.set()` when fetching project data.
    89	
    90	---
    91	
    92	## 6. CSS Theming System
    93	
    94	- All colors are defined as CSS custom properties on `:root`.
    95	- Dark mode overrides properties under `[data-theme="dark"]`.
    96	- Hard-coded hex values in dark overrides are acceptable (and necessary for specific badge backgrounds).
    97	- Never use hard-coded colors in the light-theme base styles — always reference `var(--color-*)`.
    98	- The `theme-init.js` script in `<head>` prevents FOUC by setting the attribute before body renders.
    99	
   100	---

1	# Public API Surface — MCP Server GUI
     2	
     3	---
     4	
     5	## 1. Backend REST API
     6	
     7	All routes are prefixed with `/api`. Response envelope on success: raw JSON value. Error envelope: `{ error: { code, message } }`.
     8	
     9	### Error Codes → HTTP Status
    10	
    11	| Code | Status |
    12	|------|--------|
    13	| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
    14	| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 |
    15	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
    16	| `CONFLICT` | 409 |
    17	| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 |
    18	| *(unhandled)* | 500 |
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	### 1.1 Projects
    23	
    24	| Method | Path | Handler | Description |
    25	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
    26	| `GET` | `/api/projects` | `handleListProjects` | Paginated list with filtering, sorting, search. |
    27	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug` | `handleGetProject` | Full project detail (root index + meta). |
    28	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/plan` | `handleGetPlanDocument` | Plan Markdown content. |
    29	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/synthesis` | `handleGetSynthesisDocument` | Synthesis Markdown content. |
    30	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/health` | `handleGetProjectHealth` | Health summary. |
    31	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/run-metadata` | `handleGetRunMetadata` | `.orchestrator-run.json` sidecar. |
    32	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/work-packages` | `handleListWorkPackages` | All WPs for a project. |
    33	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/work-packages/overview` | `handleGetWorkPackageOverview` | Aggregate WP status summary. |
    34	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/work-packages/:wpId` | `handleGetWorkPackage` | Single WP detail. |
    35	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/dialogues` | `handleListDialogues` | Dialogue file list (optional `?wp=` filter). |
    36	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/dialogues/:filename` | `handleGetDialogueFile` | Single dialogue content. |
    37	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks` | `handleListChunks` | Chunk file list (optional `?wp=` filter). |
    38	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename` | `handleGetChunkFile` | Raw chunk JSONL content. |
    39	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/rendered` | `handleGetChunkFile` + `renderChunksToDialogue` / `renderChunksToStructured` | Rendered chunk. Without `?format=structured`: Markdown string (`{ content }`) — compact chat-like format, plain paragraphs, per-tool summaries. With `?format=structured`: JSON array (`{ blocks: DialogueBlock[] }`) for interactive frontend rendering. |
    40	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/runs` | `handleListRunLogs` | Orchestrator run log file list. |
    41	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/runs/:filename` | `handleGetRunLog` | Log entries (supports `?after=N` for streaming). |
    42	| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug` | `handleDeleteProject` | Permanently delete a project. |
    43	| `PATCH` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug` | `handleRenameProject` | Rename title or slug. Body: `{ title?: string, slug?: string }`. |
    44	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/archive` | `handleArchiveProject` | Set status to ARCHIVED. |
    45	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/unarchive` | `handleUnarchiveProject` | Restore from ARCHIVED. |
    46	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/complete` | `handleMarkProjectComplete` | Mark project COMPLETE. |
    47	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:repo/:slug/reset` | `handleResetProject` | Reset project (dry_run or apply). Body: `{ dry_run: boolean, decisions?: [] }`. |
    48	
    49	#### GET /api/projects Query Parameters
    50	
    51	| Param | Type | Default | Description |
    52	|-------|------|---------|-------------|
    53	| `page` | number | 1 | Page number (1-indexed). |
    54	| `limit` | number | 50 | Items per page (max 200). |
    55	| `status` | string | `'ACTIVE'` | `'ACTIVE'`, `'ALL'`, or a specific status value. |
    56	| `search` | string | — | Case-insensitive substring match on slug, name, repo. |
    57	| `sort` | string | `'last_updated'` | Column: `project`, `repository`, `status`, `total_work_packages`, `done`, `date_created`, `last_updated`, `runner`. |
    58	| `dir` | string | `'desc'` | `'asc'` or `'desc'`. |
    59	| `runner` | string | — | Filter: `'orchestrator'`, `'vscode'`, `'claude-code'`, `'unknown'`. |
    60	
    61	#### GET /api/projects Response Envelope (`ProjectListEnvelope`)
    62	
    63	```typescript
    64	{
    65	  projects: ProjectSummary[];
    66	  total: number;
    67	  page: number;
    68	  limit: number;
    69	  total_pages: number;
    70	  status_counts: Record<string, number>;
    71	  runner_counts: Record<string, number>;
    72	}
    73	```
    74	
    75	---
    76	
    77	### 1.2 Orchestrator
    78	
    79	| Method | Path | Handler | Description |
    80	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
    81	| `GET` | `/api/orchestrator/queue` | `handleGetOrchestratorQueue` | Current queue entries with effective status. |
    82	| `GET` | `/api/orchestrator/run-status/:filename` | `handleGetRunStatus` | Status from a specific log file. |
    83	| `POST` | `/api/orchestrator/start` | `handleOrchestratorStart` | Run preflight + spawn orchestrator. Body: `{ planPath, dryRun?, resumeThreadId? }`. |
    84	| `POST` | `/api/orchestrator/kill/:id` | `handleOrchestratorKill` | SIGTERM → SIGKILL escalation. |
    85	| `POST` | `/api/orchestrator/dismiss/:id` | `handleOrchestratorDismiss` | Remove dead entry from queue. Returns 204. |
    86	
    87	---
    88	
    89	### 1.3 Knowledge
    90	
    91	| Method | Path | Handler | Description |
    92	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
    93	| `GET` | `/api/knowledge` | `handleListKnowledge` | List/search insights. Query: `?scope&category&tags&repository_name&query&limit&offset`. |
    94	| `PATCH` | `/api/knowledge/:id` | `handleUpdateKnowledge` | Update insight fields. Body validated by `KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema`. |
    95	| `DELETE` | `/api/knowledge/:id` | `handleDeleteKnowledge` | Delete insight. Query: `?scope&repository_name`. |
    96	| `POST` | `/api/knowledge/:id/promote` | `handlePromoteKnowledge` | Promote repository insight to global. Query: `?scope&repository_name`. |

101	### 1.4 Model Registry
   102	
   103	All routes are handled by `api-models.ts` and are registered in the declarative `buildRoutes()` table — dispatched by `dispatchRoute()` along with every other API route.
   104	
   105	| Method | Path | Handler | Description |
   106	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
   107	| `GET` | `/api/models` | `handleGetModels` | Returns model list. Auto-initializes `local.json` from `default.json` on first access. |
   108	| `PUT` | `/api/models` | `handleSaveModels` | Bulk-save the model list. Auto-assigns UUIDv4 to entries without `id`. Returns 409 when a deletion would remove a referenced model. |
   109	| `POST` | `/api/models/load-defaults` | `handleLoadDefaults` | Merge `default.json` into `local.json` without overwriting existing entries. Returns `{ models, conflicts }`. |
   110	
   111	#### PUT /api/models Request Body
   112	
   113	Array of model entries validated by `SaveModelsBodySchema`:
   114	
   115	```typescript
   116	Array<{
   117	  id?: string;          // UUIDv4 — omit to auto-assign
   118	  name: string;         // Display name (min 1 char)
   119	  slug: string;         // Lowercase kebab-case (regex: /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/)
   120	  cc_model?: string;    // Claude Code model identifier (default: "inherit")
   121	}>
   122	```
   123	
   124	**Validation rules:**
   125	- Duplicate `slug` values → 400
   126	- Reserved slug `"inherit"` on a non-sentinel entry → 400
   127	- Removing a model that is referenced in assignments → 409 with `referencedModels` details (user must use Replace Model first)
   128	
   129	#### PUT /api/models Response
   130	
   131	```typescript
   132	// Success
   133	{ models: ModelEntry[] }
   134	
   135	// 409 Conflict (referenced model deletion blocked)
   136	{
   137	  conflict: true;
   138	  referencedModels: Array<{ model: ModelEntry; usages: string[] }>;
   139	}
   140	```
   141	
   142	---
   143	
   144	### 1.5 Model Assignments
   145	
   146	| Method | Path | Handler | Description |
   147	|--------|------|---------|-------------|
   148	| `GET` | `/api/model-assignments` | `handleGetAssignments` | Returns assignments enriched with `stale` boolean. |
   149	| `PUT` | `/api/model-assignments` | `handleUpdateAssignments` | Validate and persist assignments. Returns 400 when `name-mapping.json` is absent or invalid. |
   150	| `POST` | `/api/model-assignments/replace` | `handleReplaceAssignedModel` | Swap all occurrences of `old_model_id` with `new_model_id`. Returns 400 for same-model swap or unreferenced source. |
   151	
   152	#### GET /api/model-assignments Response
   153	
   154	```typescript
   155	{
   156	  default_model_uuid?: string;              // Optional global default
   157	  persona_models: Record<string, string>;   // Persona ID → model UUID
   158	  stale: boolean;                           // See staleness rules below
   159	}
   160	```
   161	
   162	**Staleness rules for `stale`:**
   163	
   164	| Condition | `stale` |
   165	|-----------|---------|
   166	| `max(mtime(assignments.json), mtime(local.json))` > `mtime(name-mapping.json)` | `true` — rebuild needed |
   167	| Neither `assignments.json` nor `local.json` exist | `false` — no user changes yet |
   168	| `name-mapping.json` does not exist | `false` — no build output to compare |
   169	| Only `default.json` is newer than `name-mapping.json` | `false` — Git checkout mtime, not a user change |
   170	
   171	#### PUT /api/model-assignments Request Body
   172	
   173	```typescript
   174	{
   175	  default_model_uuid?: string;             // Must exist in model registry if provided
   176	  persona_models: Record<string, string>;  // Key: persona id from name-mapping.json; Value: model UUID
   177	}
   178	```
   179	
   180	**Validation rules:**
   181	- `name-mapping.json` must exist → 400 if absent
   182	- All persona keys in `persona_models` must appear as `id` values in `name-mapping.json` → 400 if invalid
   183	- All model UUIDs (including `default_model_uuid`) must exist in the registry → 400 if not found
   184	
   185	#### POST /api/model-assignments/replace Request Body
   186	
   187	```typescript
   188	{ old_model_id: string; new_model_id: string }  // Both must be UUIDs in registry
   189	```
   190	
   191	**Rejection conditions (400):**
   192	- `old_model_id === new_model_id` — "Source and target models must be different"
   193	- `old_model_id` not referenced in any assignment — "Model is not referenced in any current assignment"

101	project-detail-helpers.js   — pure helpers; no dependencies on other project-detail files
   102	  ↓
   103	project-detail-orch.js      — orchestrator section; depends on helpers
   104	  ↓

   108	```
   109	
   110	**Shared-state invariant:** `_pdLogPreviewCleanups` is declared and initialised as a `var` in `project-detail.js` and immediately promoted to `globalThis._pdLogPreviewCleanups` so that `project-detail-orch.js` can push cleanups into, and drain, the same array instance. Both drain sites use `.length = 0` (in-place mutation). A `= []` reassignment would break array identity across the module boundary — see `constraints.md §3`.
   111	
   112	---
   113	
   114	## 4. Hash-Based Routing
   115	
   116	```
   117	User clicks link or navigates
   118	  │
   119	  └── hashchange event fires
   120	      │
   121	      └── Router.dispatch(window.location.hash)
   122	          ├── Clear any active polling interval
   123	          ├── Update nav link .active state
   124	          ├── Match hash against route patterns:
   125	          │   ├── "/" or ""                          → renderProjectList(app)
   126	          │   ├── /projects/:repo/:slug/plan        → renderPlan(app, repo, slug)
   127	          │   ├── /projects/:repo/:slug/synthesis   → renderSynthesis(app, repo, slug)
   128	          │   ├── /projects/:repo/:slug             → renderProjectDetail(app, repo, slug)
   129	          │   ├── /projects/:repo/:slug/wp/:wpId    → renderWorkPackageDetail(app, repo, slug, wpId)
   130	          │   ├── /projects/:repo/:slug/runs/:file  → renderRunLog(app, repo, slug, file)
   131	          │   ├── /config                           → renderConfig(app)
   132	          │   ├── /insights                         → renderInsights(app)
   133	          │   ├── /knowledge                        → renderKnowledge(app)
   134	          │   ├── /orchestrator                     → renderOrchestrator(app)
   135	          │   └── (no match)                        → error banner "Page not found"
   136	          └── View render function:
   137	              ├── showLoading(app)
   138	              ├── Fetch data via API.*
   139	              ├── Build HTML string
   140	              ├── Set app.innerHTML = html
   141	              └── (Optional) Set up polling via Router._setPolling()
   142	```
   143	
   144	---
   145	
   146	## 5. Stale Instance Detection
   147	
   148	```
   149	StaleCheck.init()
   150	  └── setInterval(30s):
   151	      ├── GET /api/server-info
   152	      │   → { stale, bootVersions, diskVersions }
   153	      │
   154	      ├── If stale === false → no action
   155	      │
   156	      └── If stale === true:
   157	          ├── Stop polling (one-shot detection)
   158	          ├── Compare boot vs disk per component
   159	          │   (mcpServer, personas, orchestrator)
   160	          └── Insert sticky .stale-banner at top of <body>
   161	              with list of changed components
   162	```
   163	
   164	---
   165	
   166	## 6. Orchestrator Queue Flow
   167	
   168	```
   169	GET /api/orchestrator/queue
   170	  │
   171	  └── getQueue(logsDir, ledgerRoot)
   172	      ├── readQueueFile(logsDir) → RawQueueEntry[]
   173	      ├── For each entry:
   174	      │   ├── isProcessAlive(pid) → boolean
   175	      │   ├── getProjectLedgerStatus(slug, repo?, ledgerRoot) → ledger exists?
   176	      │   ├── computeEffectiveStatus(raw, alive, hasProject, stageActivity)
   177	      │   │   → 'pending' | 'started' | 'dead'
   178	      │   └── Exclude if synthesis_generated === true (AC-6)
   179	      └── Return QueueEntry[] with effectiveStatus + enrichment
   180	
   181	POST /api/orchestrator/start
   182	  │
   183	  ├── Validate body: { planPath, dryRun?, resumeThreadId? }
   184	  ├── Run 7 preflight checks (venv, dist, .env, no lock, etc.)
   185	  │   → PreflightResult[]
   186	  ├── If any check fails → return { ok: false, preflight: [...] }
   187	  └── If all pass:
   188	      ├── Spawn detached python orchestrator process
   189	      └── Return { ok: true, preflight: [...], pid }
   190	
   191	POST /api/orchestrator/kill/:id
   192	  │
   193	  ├── Find queue entry by id
   194	  ├── Send SIGTERM to pid
   195	  ├── Wait 3s
   196	  ├── If still alive → SIGKILL
   197	  ├── Remove .orchestrator.lock
   198	  └── Remove entry from queue file (atomic write)
   199	```

101	
   102	## 7. Security Constraints (Backend)
   103	
   104	### Path Traversal Prevention
   105	
   106	- All URL path parameters (slug, repo, wpId, filename) are validated against allowlist regexes before filesystem access.
   107	- `SAFE_SLUG_REGEX` (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`) for project slugs and repo names.
   108	- `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*$/`) for WP IDs and queue entry IDs.
   109	- Static file serving checks `resolve(filePath).startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR)`.
   110	- Invalid parameters always return `NOT_FOUND` — never a different error that could leak information.
   111	
   112	### Body Size Limit
   113	
   114	- `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1_048_576` (1 MiB) enforced by `readBody()`.
   115	- Both `Content-Length` pre-check and streaming byte-count check.
   116	- Exceeding the limit throws `PayloadTooLargeError` → HTTP 413.
   117	
   118	### Information Hiding
   119	
   120	- Ambiguous slug resolutions are downgraded to NOT_FOUND (cross-namespace existence leak prevention).
   121	- Malformed `.meta.json` files log to stderr but return NOT_FOUND to clients.
   122	- Error responses never include internal paths or stack traces.
   123	
   124	### Security Headers
   125	
   126	All responses include:
   127	- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
   128	- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
   129	- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
   130	- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`
   131	
   132	---
   133	
   134	## 8. STDIO Discipline
   135	
   136	- **`server.ts`**: May write to stdout (it runs as a standalone process, not an MCP server).
   137	- **`api.ts`, `api-knowledge.ts`, `orchestrator-manager.ts`**: Never write to `process.stdout`. Diagnostics go to `process.stderr` only.
   138	- **Rationale:** The MCP server communicates via stdout. Although the GUI is a separate process, handler files are shared — keeping them stdout-free prevents accidental protocol corruption if handlers are ever loaded in the MCP process.
   139	
   140	---
   141	
   142	## 9. Route Dispatch Ordering
   143	
   144	Routes in `server.ts` `matchRoute()` are matched by **segment count first**, then by segment values in declaration order. When adding new routes:
   145	
   146	- More-specific patterns must appear BEFORE catch-all patterns at the same segment count.
   147	- Use explicit keyword exclusion arrays (`rest[2] !== 'plan' && ...`) to prevent shadowing.
   148	- Namespaced routes (`/:repo/:slug/...`) and legacy flat routes (`/:slug/...`) coexist — the namespaced versions appear after the flat ones.
   149	
   150	---
   151	
   152	## 10. Deprecated Route Convention
   153	
   154	Legacy non-namespaced routes (e.g., `/api/projects/:slug`) are retained for backward compatibility and marked with `@deprecated` comments. Each deprecated route has a comment pointing to its namespaced replacement. These will be removed in the next major version.
   155	
   156	---
   157	
   158	## 11. Polling Convention
   159	
   160	- Views that need live data set up polling via `Router._setPolling(fn, delayMs)`.
   161	- The router **automatically clears** any active interval on route change.
   162	- The `OrchestratorWidgets.renderLogPreview()` returns a cleanup function for component-level polling. Callers must wrap the push with `if (cleanup)` to defend against a null/undefined return (the current implementation always returns a function, but the guard is kept for contract safety).
   163	- Default intervals: 3–5 seconds for active data, 30 seconds for stale checks.
   164	- **In-place patch pattern (project-detail):** `renderProjectDetail` avoids full-page rebuilds on poll ticks by comparing a stable structure key (`_orchRunsStructureKey`) against the previous tick. If the structure is unchanged, only the status card's `innerHTML` is replaced (`_patchOrchStatusCard`). If the structure changed (new run, run completed, or first tick), a full `renderRunsList` is performed with scroll-position save/restore. See `data-flows.md §9` for details.
   165	
   166	---
   167	
   168	## 12. Error Handling Convention (Frontend)
   169	
   170	- API errors are caught and displayed via `showError(container, message)`.
   171	- Error objects have shape `{ code: string, message: string }`.
   172	- `window.alert()` is used for action failures (kill, dismiss) where the page shouldn't navigate.
   173	- `window.confirm()` gates destructive actions (kill, delete).
   174	
   175	---
   176	
   177	## 13. HTML Generation Convention
   178	
   179	- Views build HTML as concatenated strings (not DOM manipulation).
   180	- Set `container.innerHTML = htmlString` in one assignment.
   181	- Use `escapeHtml()` for ALL user-provided text to prevent XSS.
   182	- Never use `innerHTML` with unescaped user data.
   183	- DOM event listeners (for buttons, forms) are attached AFTER innerHTML is set, using `querySelector` / `getElementById`.
   184	
   185	---
   186	
   187	## 14. Version Busting Convention
   188	
   189	Script and stylesheet references in `index.html` use `?v=N` query parameters for cache busting:
   190	
   191	```html
   192	<script src="/api-client.js?v=3"></script>
   193	```
   194	
   195	When modifying a frontend file, increment its `?v=N` parameter in `index.html` to ensure browsers pick up the change.
   196	
   197	---
   198	
   199	## 15. Dual-Format Endpoint Pattern (`?format=structured`)
   200

201	Some backend endpoints support a `?format=structured` query parameter to switch the response
   202	between a plain-text format and a structured JSON format without breaking existing callers.
   203	
   204	**Current endpoints using this pattern:**
   205	
   206	| Endpoint | Without parameter | With `?format=structured` |
   207	|----------|-------------------|---------------------------|
   208	| `GET …/chunks/:filename/rendered` | `{ content: string }` — Markdown from `renderChunksToDialogue()` | `{ blocks: DialogueBlock[] }` — typed array from `renderChunksToStructured()` |
   209	
   210	**Rules for this pattern:**
   211	
   212	1. **Backward-compatible by default.** Omitting the parameter always returns the legacy format.
   213	   Existing callers do not need to be updated.
   214	2. **Format detection is via `URLSearchParams`.** Use
   215	   `new URLSearchParams(qStr).get('format') === 'structured'` — do not parse manually.
   216	3. **Only `format=structured` is a valid structured-mode value.** Any other value falls back to the
   217	   default format; no error is returned for unknown values.
   218	4. **New dual-format endpoints must document both response shapes** in `api-surface.md`
   219	   (routes table row) and the corresponding data flow in `data-flows.md`.
   220	
   221	---
   222	
   223	## 16. Known Limitations
   224	
   225	| Limitation | Impact |
   226	|------------|--------|
   227	| No hot reload | Must manually refresh browser after frontend changes. |
   228	| No TypeScript on frontend | No type checking for client-side code. |
   229	| Single-threaded server | No worker threads; long handler blocking affects all requests. |
   230	| No WebSocket | Polling-based updates only; no push notifications. |
   231	| CORS locked to localhost | Cannot access from remote machines without modification. |
   232	| Queue file locking gap | TypeScript uses atomic rename; Python uses `.run-queue.lock`. Concurrent writes could race (low risk). |
   233	| No authentication | Local development tool; assumes trusted network. |

   251	### `chunk-accumulator.ts` — Shared accumulation layer
   252	
   253	Pure-function module. No I/O, no side effects, no imports from `mcp-server/src/`. All exports are named.
   254	
   255	#### Types
   256	
   257	| Export | Kind | Description |
   258	|--------|------|-------------|
   259	| `JsonValue` | `type` | Raw JSON value accepted in chunk payloads. |
   260	| `ToolCallChunk` | `interface` | Single tool-call fragment from an `AIMessageChunk`. Fields: `index?`, `id?`, `name?`, `args?`. |
   261	| `MergedToolCall` | `interface` | Accumulated tool call (after merging). Fields: `id`, `name`, `args`. |
   262	| `ContentBlock` | `interface` | Content block (text or non-text). Fields: `type`, `text?`, index signature. |
   263	| `MergedMessage` | `interface` | Merged/reconstructed message. Fields: `type`, `id`, `content`, `tool_calls`, `usage_metadata`, `tool_call_id?`. |
   264	| `NamespaceKey` | `type` | `string` — `""` for main agent, `"subgraph/node"` for sub-agents. |
   265	
   266	#### Functions
   267	
   268	| Export | Signature | Description |
   269	|--------|-----------|-------------|
   270	| `chunkId` | `(chunk: Record<string, JsonValue>) → string` | Extracts the stable `id` field from a chunk payload. |
   271	| `chunkType` | `(chunk: Record<string, JsonValue>) → string` | Returns the `type` field from a chunk payload. |
   272	| `mergeContent` | `(acc, incoming) → string \| ContentBlock[]` | Merges a new content value into an accumulated content value (string concat or block-list merge). |
   273	| `mergeToolCallChunks` | `(acc: Map<number, MergedToolCall>, chunks: ToolCallChunk[]) → void` | Merges `tool_call_chunks` fragments into an accumulator map keyed by index. |
   274	| `mergeUsageMetadata` | `(acc, incoming) → Record<string, number>` | Sums `usage_metadata` numeric fields into an accumulator. |
   275	| `isValidHeader` | `(line: string) → boolean` | Validates that a JSONL line is a `chunk_format: 1` header. |
   276	| `parseChunkLine` | `(line: string) → { namespace, msg, metadata } \| null` | Parses one JSONL data line (object or array shape). Returns `null` on parse errors. |
   277	| `namespaceKey` | `(ns: string[]) → NamespaceKey` | Converts a raw namespace array to a display key (`""` for main agent). |
   278	| `namespaceLabel` | `(key: NamespaceKey) → string` | Returns a human-readable label (`"Main Agent"` or the key string). |
   279	| `accumulateChunks` | `(records: Array<{ namespace, msg }>) → Map<NamespaceKey, MergedMessage[]>` | Accumulates parsed chunk records into a namespace-keyed map of merged messages. |
   280	
   281	### `chunk-renderer.ts` — Rendering layer
   282	
   283	Imports all types and functions from `chunk-accumulator.ts`. Exports three pure renderers and the `DialogueBlock` discriminated union type:
   284	
   285	| Export | Signature | Description |
   286	|--------|-----------|-------------|
   287	| `renderChunksToMarkdown` | `(jsonlContent: string) → string` | Verbose format: `## Role` headings, JSON fenced tool-call blocks, token-usage footer. |
   288	| `renderChunksToDialogue` | `(jsonlContent: string) → string` | Compact chat-like format: plain-paragraph AI text, per-tool summary lines, hidden ToolMessages, sub-agent `### Subagent:` headings. |
   289	| `renderChunksToStructured` | `(jsonlContent: string) → DialogueBlock[]` | Structured format: returns a typed JSON array of `DialogueBlock` objects for interactive frontend rendering. |
   290	| `DialogueBlock` | *(exported type)* | Discriminated union describing one rendered block in the structured view. |
   291	
   292	#### `DialogueBlock` Type
   293	
   294	```typescript
   295	type DialogueBlock =
   296	  | { type: 'text'; content: string }
   297	  | { type: 'tool-call'; name: string; detailLines: string[]; args: unknown; result?: { content: string } }
   298	  | { type: 'subagent-heading'; label: string }
   299	  | { type: 'checklist'; items: Array<{ content: string; status: string; checked: boolean }> };
   300	```
   301	
   302	Variants:
   303	- `text` — A prose paragraph of AI-generated text.
   304	- `tool-call` — One tool invocation: name, summary detail lines, parsed args JSON, and an optional embedded ToolMessage result for non-inline tools (e.g. `read_file`, `ledger_*`).
   305	- `subagent-heading` — Heading marking the start of a sub-agent namespace.
   306	- `checklist` — A `write_todos` invocation rendered as a typed item list; each item carries `content`, `status`, and a pre-computed `checked` boolean.
